text.title: New Dependency Risk Checklist — Procedure
text.summary: Nine steps that turn "npm install foo" into a risk record: check the lockfile for the package, read the SPDX licence, count the transitive subtree with a dry run, read maintainers and release date, run the dated advisory lookup, review install hooks and provenance, list alternatives including in-house, pin the exact version with the lockfile commit, then decide and route the alert to the owner.

step.name: check-already-in-tree
step.input: The committed lockfile; the package name and the exact version proposed.
step.action: Search the lockfile for the package at the same major version. Record `package.name`, `version` (exact, from the registry), `ecosystem`.
step.decision-gate: Already in tree at the same major: skip this methodology; import from the existing version (06 root question). No committed lockfile: stop until one exists (r-exact-version-pinned-in-lockfile).

step.name: read-spdx-licence
step.input: `license` in package.json / `project.license` in pyproject.toml / `license` in Cargo.toml; the LICENSE file in the source repository.
step.action: Record the SPDX identifier as the `licence` input; if metadata and LICENSE disagree, record the LICENSE file's identifier and note the mismatch in `decision.statement`. For GPL-*, AGPL-*, LGPL-*, SSPL, BUSL or modified MPL-2.0, set the `distribution_model` input and `decision.distribution_model`.
step.decision-gate: `unknown`, `see repo`, `MIT-ish` or empty stops the record (r-licence-spdx-recorded).

step.name: count-transitive-subtree
step.input: `npm install --package-lock-only` then a lockfile diff; `pip install --dry-run --report`; `cargo tree --prefix none | sort -u`.
step.action: Record the number of packages added beyond the direct one as `transitive_count`.
step.decision-gate: Zero on a package that imports other packages is an unfilled field; re-run the dry run (r-transitive-footprint-counted).

step.name: read-maintainers-and-recency
step.input: `npm view <pkg> maintainers`, the PyPI project page, crates.io owners; the latest non-prerelease date.
step.decision-gate: One maintainer or a release older than 12 months requires `decision.fallback` (vendor, fork or a named alternative) before any accept (r-maintainer-and-release-recency).

step.name: run-advisory-lookup
step.input: OSV.dev, the GitHub Advisory Database or NVD, queried for the exact name and version today.
step.action: Record `advisory_lookup.source`, `url`, `checked_on`, `open_advisories[]`; add the URL to `evidence[]`. Run `npm audit` / `pip-audit` / `cargo audit` on the lockfile so the subtree is covered too.
step.decision-gate: An open, unpatched advisory forces `reject` or `accept-with-mitigation` naming the id (r-advisory-query-in-evidence).

step.name: review-hooks-and-provenance
step.input: `npm view <pkg> scripts`; the registry `repository` field; the README's repository link; a registry search for the name with one character changed.
step.action: Fill `package.install_scripts` (each hook and what it runs), `registry_repository_url`, `readme_repository_url`, `repository_matches`, `near_name.searched`, `near_name.popular_near_name`.
step.decision-gate: A near-name of a far more popular package, a repository mismatch, or a hook that fetches a remote binary is a reject unless `decision.install_hook_reason` says why it is needed (r-install-hooks-and-provenance-reviewed).

step.name: list-alternatives-including-in-house
step.input: The package's exported surface; the current lockfile; the registry.
step.action: Record `alternative` with at least one entry and always `in-house` or `already-in-tree`, each with a one-line reason; record `useful_surface_lines` when the package is small.
step.decision-gate: A useful surface of 20 lines or fewer defaults to `verdict: in-house`; overriding needs `decision.override_reason` (r-alternative-considered-including-in-house).

step.name: pin-version-and-lockfile
step.input: The PR that adds the dependency.
step.action: Confirm the manifest pins the exact version and the lockfile diff is committed; record `lockfile.file` and `lockfile.commit_url`; add the URL to `evidence[]`.
step.decision-gate: A range (`^`, `~`, `>=`) in the manifest or no lockfile commit blocks approval (r-exact-version-pinned-in-lockfile).

step.name: decide-and-route-alerts
step.input: All inputs; the Dependabot / Renovate / audit configuration.
step.action: Write `decision.verdict` and `statement` naming `name@version`; add `fallback`, `mitigation`, `distribution_model`, `override_reason`, `install_hook_reason` where the gates above require them. Set `patch_window` (`critical`, `high`), `alert_routing.tool` and `recipient` = `owner`, `review.next_review_at`. Fill `templates/skeleton.md.j2`; run `scripts/validate-new-dependency-risk-checklist.py --file`; the owner reads the advisory and licence lines before the lockfile change merges.
step.output: Committed risk record; alert routed to the owner.
step.decision-gate: An owner with no alert routed to them, or no patch window, is unfilled (r-upgrade-owner-and-patch-window, 03 human checkpoint).

list.item: Record validates via `scripts/validate-new-dependency-risk-checklist.py`, including the 12-month, single-maintainer, advisory and 20-line cross-field checks.
`evidence[]` carries the dated advisory URL and the lockfile commit.
The owner is the alert recipient and has read the record before merge.
